title: dynamic-batching: adaptive sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: production workloads show high padding overhead on mixed-length request distributions (chat + long-context completion). This PR implements adaptive sequence-length bucketing and a padding-minimization scheduler to reduce token waste while preserving latency SLOs.
Key ideas: 1) Maintain a short-term histogram of request sequence lengths and compute bucket boundaries at tunable percentiles (default: 10/30/60/90). 2) Group incoming requests into buckets by current boundaries and form batches within buckets to maximize kernel efficiency and minimize padding. 3) When needed for latency SLOs, opportunistically pack short requests together using an in-batch reordering heuristic that preserves per-request order semantics while improving utilization. 4) Add conservative safety checks: per-batch estimated latency model and batch admission controller that enforces SLO headroom; automatic fallback to single-bucket batching if latency risk is detected. 5) Integrate with KV cache reuse: requests in the same bucket prefer co-location to maximize KV cache hit rates; added heuristics to avoid cache thrashing when buckets are rebalanced.
What changed (high level): - New runtime components: runtime/batcher/seqlen_histogram.{cpp,h}, runtime/batcher/bucketing_scheduler.{cpp,h}, runtime/batcher/padding_optimizer.{cpp,h} - Kernel selection changes: runtime/kernel_selector.cpp updated to prefer kernels optimized for the bucketed max-seqlen and to re-evaluate kernel choice when bucket boundaries change. - Continuous batching loop: adjusted to consult the adaptive buckets and to expose batch-formation diagnostics. - Metrics and observability: added metrics: batching_bucket_counts, batching_padding_ratio, batch_estimated_latency, kv_cache_colocation_ratio. Added tracing spans for bucket assignment and padding optimization decisions. - Configuration: added runtime config options batcher.adaptive.enabled, batcher.adaptive.window_ms, batcher.adaptive.percentiles, batcher.adaptive.max_bucket_count, batcher.adaptive.latency_headroom_ms. - Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for histogram and bucket update logic; integration perf benchmark in tests/bench/dynamic_batching_bench.py; canary job updated to exercise mixed workload (chat + long completion).
Backwards compatibility: feature is opt-in (batcher.adaptive.enabled=false by default) and falls back to existing fixed-bucketing behavior.
Performance summary (perf-canary): on a mixed workload trace (30% long >1024 tokens, 60% short <128, 10% medium) we observed: - token-cost reduction (measured by average per-token GPU cycles) ~12% (95% CI: ±1.6%) - p95 token latency improvement ~9% - padding ratio reduced from 42% -> 19% - KV cache colocation ratio improved by ~5 percentage points

Implementation notes and tradeoffs (single-line sections kept continuous): - Bucketing boundaries are computed using exponentially-weighted moving percentiles to adapt quickly to workload shifts while avoiding oscillation; window size is configurable. - Bucket rebalancing is rate-limited and emits a trace; requests are not re-assigned mid-generation to avoid correctness issues. - Padding-minimizer uses lightweight integer packing heuristics and avoids heavy combinatorial scheduling to keep CPU overhead minimal. - Kernel selection is conservative: we only switch to a different kernel if the estimated speedup outweighs the cost of switching and reconfiguration. - SLO safety: admission controller uses an empirical latency model derived from historical batches; this prevents pathological cases where packing increases end-to-end latency for tail requests.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced in ENG-7842 - [x] Unit tests for histogram and scheduler - [x] Integration perf bench and canary - [x] Metrics + tracing added - [x] Config flags and sensible defaults - [x] Docs/ops guidance updated - [x] Rollout plan included

release_notes: Add opt-in adaptive sequence-length bucketing to reduce padding and improve throughput. Config flags: batcher.adaptive.*. Disabled by default; see docs/ops/dynamic_batching.md for rollout and telemetry.
notes: This change is opt-in and gated behind runtime flags. Observability added so teams can safely evaluate impact in production canaries. We plan to monitor padding_ratio and batch_estimated_latency closely during the first two weeks after rollout.
bench_results: mixed workload canary (10 runs): token-cost -12% (±1.6%), p95 token latency -9%
how_to_roll_out: Start with batcher.adaptive.enabled=false. Enable in canary clusters with batcher.adaptive.max_bucket_count=4 and percentiles=10,30,60,90. Monitor metrics batching_padding_ratio and batch_estimated_latency; if p95 latency increases, disable packing (batcher.adaptive.disable_packing=true) and increase window_ms. Ops doc (docs/ops/dynamic_batching.md) contains guided steps, telemetry to watch, and rollback instructions.
